messages.subject: latent field outside the 95% simulations..
parts:
Dear INLA community, 

I'm running this model: 
Stk <- inla.stack(tag = "Fit",
                   data = list(y = round(totperstation$Weight)),
                   A = list(1,1,1,A),
                   effects = list(Intercept=rep(1,N),
                     X = X,
                     fSurvey = totperstation$fSurvey,
                     w = w.index))

f1 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + offset(log(Dist/Fraction)) + f(w, model = spde) + f(fSurvey, model ="iid")

M1_Zinb1 <- inla(eval(f1),
           family = "zeroinflatednbinomial1",
           data = inla.stack.data(Stk),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,
                                  waic = TRUE,
                                  config = TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(Stk)), verbose = F).

Than I determine the weight of the latent field: 
w.pm1 <- M1_Zinb1$summary.random$w$"0.5quant" #median

#spatial field
wproj <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh,  dims = c(1000, 1000))
w.pm100_100 <- inla.mesh.project(wproj, w.pm1)

Grid <- expand.grid(Lon = wproj$x,
                    Lat = wproj$y)
Grid$w.pm <- as.vector(w.pm100_100)
Grid <- Grid[!is.na(Grid$w.pm),]

#weight predicted, in which survey effect of RWS31144108
Grid$weight <- exp(Grid$w.pm + M1_Zinb1$summary.fixed[[1]][1]  + log(50/1) + M1_Zinb1$summary.random$fSurvey[M1_Zinb1$summary.random$fSurvey$ID == "2019feb_187",]$mean) 

And I determine the 95%CI: 
NSim <- 1000
SimData <- inla.posterior.sample(n = NSim, result = M1_Zinb1)
for (i in c(1:1000)) {  
w.sim <- SimData[[i]]$latent[RowNum.w]
wproj <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh,  dims = c(1000, 1000))
w.pm100_100 <- inla.mesh.project(wproj, w.sim)
Grid[[paste0("w.pm", i)]] <- as.vector(w.pm100_100)
    Betas           <- SimData[[i]]$latent[BetaRows]
    column_name     <- paste0("w.pm", i)
    w               <- Grid[Grid$inside_doggerbank == T, column_name]
    survey          <- SimData[[i]]$latent[RowNum.Survey][12] #survey 2019Feb_187
    size            <- SimData[[i]]$hyperpar[[1]]
    zero_prob       <- SimData[[i]]$hyperpar[[2]]
    mu              <- exp(Betas + w + survey + log(50))

    zero_inflation <- rbinom(n = length(mu), size = 1, prob = zero_prob)
    Y_nb <- rnbinom(n = length(mu), size = size, mu = mu)
    Dogsim[,i] <- ifelse(zero_inflation == 1, 0, Y_nb)  }


However the latent field weight falls outside the 95% CI of the simulations. What can cause this? Is the model fit not good (enough)? Or can it be something else?  
Regards, Bram Parmentier

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] latent field outside the 95% simulations..
parts:
There is no guarantee that frequenstistic properties will be satisfied in
general.

I would try to use the same procedure you're doing on a smaller and simpler
model where you can let ``n->infinity'' hence check what happens with increasing
n, if it still fail. then its likely something in your way of doing it
